initialFaculty.name: Dr. Sofia Santos
initialFaculty.motto: Demystifying algorithms one whiteboard trace at a time. Never fear recursion!
initialFaculty.education: Ph.D. in Computer Science, De La Salle University; M.S. Computer Science, UP Diliman
initialFaculty.consultationStyle: Interactive problem solving, whiteboard state tracing, high patience, and warm Earl Grey tea.
initialFaculty.consultationTip: Bring your pseudocode or a failing edge-case test. We'll trace the call stack step-by-step together!
initialFaculty.bio: Algorithms enthusiast, competitive programming mentor, and big-O notation purist. Dr. Santos has guided hundreds of students through complex graph traversals, dynamic programming hurdles, and the dreaded CCDSALG machine project. Her consultations are collaborative problem-solving sessions where students are encouraged to draw out memory states and question edge cases.

initialFaculty.name: Dr. Miguel Reyes
initialFaculty.motto: Pointers aren't scary once you can picture memory. Let's conquer the segfaults together.
initialFaculty.education: Ph.D. in Information Technology, University of Melbourne; B.S. Computer Science, DLSU (Magna Cum Laude)
initialFaculty.consultationStyle: Live code tracing, visual memory layout sketches, and friendly step-by-step GDB debugging.
initialFaculty.consultationTip: Segfault? Bring your GDB backtrace or terminal output and we'll hunt down that dangling pointer in minutes.
initialFaculty.bio: Dedicated mentor for novice programmers navigating the foundational leap into C programming. Dr. Reyes believes that wrestling with memory allocation and structs is a rite of passage, not a roadblock. Renowned for his patient debugging style, terminal workflows, and relatable analogies (like explaining linked lists using Manila train cars).

initialFaculty.name: Prof. Andrea Cruz
initialFaculty.motto: From silicon gates to global packets—understanding the physical heartbeat of computing.
subjects: Introduction to Computer Organization and Architecture 1
initialFaculty.education: Ph.D. in Electrical & Computer Engineering, NTU Singapore; B.S. Computer Engineering, DLSU
initialFaculty.consultationStyle: Hardware block diagrams, packet trace reviews, subnetting drills, and calm, authoritative guidance.
initialFaculty.consultationTip: Stuck on Wireshark captures or pipeline stalls? Grab your lab sheets and packet capture files.
initialFaculty.bio: Veteran computer architect and networking researcher with 15+ years in high-performance computing and packet-switched topologies. Prof. Cruz makes deep hardware concepts tangible, whether you're calculating subnet masks, deciphering CPU pipeline hazards, or configuring VLANs. Fiercely supportive of undergraduate research and women in systems engineering.

initialFaculty.name: Dr. Paolo Mendoza
initialFaculty.motto: Building scalable, resilient web systems that withstand real human traffic.
initialFaculty.education: Doctor of Information Technology, DLSU; Former Principal Engineer at FinTech SEA
initialFaculty.consultationStyle: Live architecture review, REST API contract inspection, DevTools network debugging, and agile code reviews.
initialFaculty.consultationTip: Have your repository branch pulled and database migrations ready. We'll inspect network requests and query latency together.
initialFaculty.bio: Practicing engineering consultant by day and passionate tech lecturer by night. Dr. Mendoza bridges academic theory with high-growth startup practices. He reviews student web architecture, RESTful API contracts, and schema designs with the eye of a veteran tech lead. A vocal champion of clean Git discipline, automated testing, and snappy frontend performance.

initialFaculty.name: Dr. Camille Garcia
initialFaculty.motto: Clean architecture is kindness to your future self. Design software crafted to last.
initialFaculty.education: Ph.D. in Software Engineering, Carnegie Mellon (Visiting Scholar) / DLSU; B.S. CS-ST
initialFaculty.consultationStyle: UML refactoring sessions, design pattern walkthroughs, code smell diagnosis, and supportive team mentorship.
initialFaculty.consultationTip: Bring your class diagrams or git commit log. We can refactor any tangled inheritance hierarchy!
initialFaculty.bio: Software engineering craftsman and OOP evangelist. Dr. Garcia champions SOLID principles, modular patterns, and comprehensive unit testing. Her consultations are celebrated for transforming messy, monolithic God objects into elegant, extensible class hierarchies. She also coaches capstone teams on agile velocity, conflict resolution, and PR etiquette.

initialFaculty.name: Prof. Rafael Domingo
initialFaculty.motto: Data always tells a story—if your schemas, indexes, and queries respect its integrity.
initialFaculty.education: Ph.D. in Computer Science, Tokyo Institute of Technology; M.S. Information Systems, DLSU
initialFaculty.consultationStyle: ERD auditing, SQL EXPLAIN plan dissection, database riddle challenges, and storytelling with a warm smile.
initialFaculty.consultationTip: Bring your ER diagram and slow SQL queries. We'll turn full table scans into lightning-fast index seeks!
initialFaculty.bio: Database guru and data modeling specialist with three decades of experience consulting on national enterprise database projects. Prof. Domingo is renowned for his humor, infectious love for 3NF normalization, and uncanny ability to spot an N+1 query problem from ten feet away. He loves helping students optimize complex SQL queries and architect robust data pipelines.
